newsitem.title: UK: UK'S TELEGRAPH, TIMES POST GAINS IN MARKET SHARE.
newsitem.headline: UK'S TELEGRAPH, TIMES POST GAINS IN MARKET SHARE.

text.p: Britain's national daily newspapers continue to battle for market share, with rivals the Daily Telegraph and the Times both posting gains in the six months from February to July, the Audit Bureau of Circulation (ABC) said on Friday.
The Daily Telegraph, owned by Hollinger Inc, gained 0.78 percentage points in the February to July period, rising to 39.26 percent from 38.47 percent a year earlier, the ABC said.
The Times, owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, saw its market share rise 0.62 percent to 26.24 percent in the 1997 six months from 25.62 percent a year-ago, the ABC said.

The Daily Telegraph, however, saw its market share slip 0.23 percent in July to 38.46 percent from 38.69 percent in June. The Time's July market share rose 0.58 percent to 26.68 percent from 26.10 percent in June, the ABC said.

The Independent, which has suffered a steady erosion in market share, posted a 1.13 percent drop in the February to July period, falling to 9.05 percent from 10.17 percent a year-earlier. But the Independent, owned by Newspapers Plc, saw its share nudge up 0.01 percent to 9.09 percent in July from 9.08 percent in June, the ABC said.

In addition, market share of Pearson Plc's Financial Times slipped 0.01 percent in the 1997 six months to 11.12 percent, while the Guardian's share dropped 0.27 percent to 14.33 percent, the ABC said.
